lines.en: Hey, Jerry, do you have a second?
Leslie, well, this is a lovely surprise.
Come on in. Have breakfast with the family.
That's okay. I just popped by to apologize
I insist you join us for breakfast.
This guy is the greatest breakfast chef in the world.
You know, I'm not really into breakfast foods.
Really? Your purse is shaped like a waffle.
The Gergich's don't take no for an answer.
Why don't you start your day?
The Gergich way with eggs, bacon, and...
Why don't you start your day?
The Gergich way with eggs, bacon, and...
But it's an extra treat because you're here to sing it with us.
Jerry, I wanted your last day at work to be special,
and I feel like I let you down.
So I made you this scrapbook with nearly four amazing pages jam-packed with memories of your time in the government.
Oh, honey, you look great in every one of these.
You are still the most handsome man in the world to me.
No, it doesn't make any sense.
Leslie, that is really sweet of you, but you don't have to worry about me.
Here, I want to show you something.
I know I didn't achieve all my work goals, but, Leslie, I don't care.
Because for me, the best part about working at the Parks Department
was that I got to be home every night with my family at 5 o'clock.
And to me, that's what mattered most.
Jerry, thank you for sharing this with me.
Room, room, room, the hug machine.
